chunks: And from him (Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad) from Al-Kahili who said: Hammadah bint Al-Hasan, the sister of Abu Ubaydah Al-Hadda', narrated to me, saying:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and stipulated for her that he would not marry another woman besides her, and she accepted that as her dowry. She said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a flawed condition; the marriage will not be valid unless it is upon a dirham or two dirhams.'

key_terms.دِرْهَم: A silver coin, used here as a unit of currency for minimum dowry
key_terms.شَرْطٌ فَاسِدٌ: A flawed/valid condition that does not invalidate the contract but has specific legal effects

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stipulating monogamy in a Shia marriage contract and what is the minimum required dowry?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a condition of monogamy is valid but does not invalidate the marriage if the husband marries again, distinguishing it from the essential requirement of a nominal dowry. He emphasizes that while the wife may accept the promise of not marrying another as her *mahr*, the contract still requires a tangible minimum value (one or two dirhams) to be legally binding, reflecting the Shia juristic view that conditions are supplementary to the core pillars of marriage. This ruling underscores the flexibility of marital conditions in Shia fiqh while maintaining the structural integrity of the contract through the dowry.
